original_clauses.source_paraphrase: The complaint alleges that nH Predict generated expected post-acute care durations and that UnitedHealthcare used those projections as practical coverage cutoffs despite contrary treating-clinician information.
original_clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: A population-derived or predictive care estimate may inform an individual entitlement decision, but it cannot itself become binding coverage authority without the independently required patient-specific decision basis.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The pleaded mechanism describes a predictive estimate being promoted from decision support into practically determinative individual coverage authority. The mapping remains provisional because the merits are contested and the court has not found that the model dictated the named denials.

original_clauses.source_paraphrase: UnitedHealthcare’s coverage documents stated that clinical services staff and physicians make decisions on health-care services, while the surviving contract theory asks whether UHC complied with that representation when plaintiffs allege AI was used instead.
original_clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Where a consequential coverage process defines a clinical/physician decision route, an alternate automated path must not displace that route unless it supplies an authorised equivalent governance effect.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The pleaded mechanism is an alternate AI-supported decision path allegedly avoiding the represented clinical/physician route. The relationship is provisional because whether that displacement occurred is still a merits question.
